public_rationale: Contemporary evaluations document frequent direct counting errors across several models. Reasonable prompting improved performance substantially, but errors remained. The qualification “reliably” matters: Codex reached 93.2% on one counting evaluation, and program execution raised another result to 96.7%. The evidence supports unreliable direct counting, not an inability to count or to build a useful counting system.
limitations: Reliability has no speaker-specified threshold; a human-comparative interpretation would give more weight to Codex's strong result.
Accuracy depends strongly on prompts and task construction.
The research papers do not specify exact experiment dates; their results are dated at year precision.
The chronology of the first counting tests is not adjudicated.

statement.excerpt: People had been testing these Ais abilities at simple arithmetic for years before it occurred to anyone to check whether they can count. (They can’t, reliably).

our_interpretation: Assess the counting assertion identified by the screens, separately from the historical assertion about when researchers first tested counting.
The plain reading is that contemporary GPT-like models frequently make mistakes when directly counting items or characters. It does not mean they never produce correct counts.
Include ordinary and step-by-step prompting. Treat execution of externally generated programs separately from the model answering directly.
For this ongoing research-state observation, use the latest completed research year and the elapsed publication year: 2022 through 17 February 2023. This observation window is evaluator-selected.
criteria.support_condition: Repeated evaluations show appreciable counting errors across contemporary GPT-like models or ordinary counting tasks, including errors that remain with reasonable prompting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show consistently dependable direct counting across varied ordinary tasks and contemporary models, with reported failures confined to unusual or misleading prompts.

evidence.locator: Table 3, Object Counting row and caption
evidence.explanation: Object-counting accuracy was 44.0%, 45.2%, and 51.2% with answer-only prompts for InstructGPT, Codex, and PaLM; step-by-step prompts raised these to 77.2%, 93.2%, and 83.2%. The Codex result exceeded the average human-rater score of 86.1%, materially limiting any claim of general counting incapacity.

The study's Codex baseline scored 37.6% with direct answers and 73.0% with step-by-step answers. The 96.7% result used generated programs and a Python interpreter, showing an effective workaround while leaving direct counting errors substantial.
